# Tales of Tibia — 469, Part 5: "Complete Madness"

- **URL:** https://article.talesoftibia.com/469/5
- **Retrieved:** 2026-09-04
- **Author:** "Simula" / s2ward
- **This is the final part.** `/469/6` returns a GitHub Pages 404.

## Archiving note

Structured reconstruction, not a verbatim mirror (see part 1 file). This part contains the reveal, so
the two load-bearing pieces of evidence are quoted exactly as the article gives them.

## Structure and argument

**§ Catastrophe.** Loose ends tied off with NPC testimony: the Cranky Lizard Crone recalls a time
when everything was bright and the waters pure before the sky darkened and everyone in her village
died in "ziz horrible cataztrophe"; she also mentions experience "from my time working for zeze
people", which the author uses to argue northern Zao was once inhabited by hat-wearing humanoids
rather than snakemen. Mr Brandon of Sunken City recalls "the... THINGS", read as ancient bonelords.

**§ Roshamuul and the Dream Catcher.** Presented as the true centre, replacing Serpentine Tower ("But
I have lied... That was sort of a lie."). Morax's quest (bring tea, sleep in his bed) leads to a
cistern resembling a dream teleporter machine, with an item that disappears between the real world and
Morax's dream. Morax on the Essence of Wishful Thinking ("very powerful… addictive… steers thoughts
and enslaves") and the Essence of Dread ("Gist of dark dreams… used mumble interrogation of test
subjects mumble strong hallucinations mumble poison").

**§ The dreamer's memoir.** A six-part first-person account, attributed by the author to a bonelord,
is quoted extensively: a being who prolonged its life with "stolen life-force and dreams" and can no
longer distinguish memory from invention; whose people's name "is nothing meant for vocal chords. It
is a thought pattern, half a dream and untranslatable into any tongue"; who were called dreamstealers,
dreamvampires and dreamshapers; who served Zathroth's side in the god wars as spies, messengers and
advisors; who mastered dream-shaping, used dreams as currency, and built **the great dream catcher**.
The memoir then recounts the trap built as a prison for the demon princes, the double-cross, the
slaughter in the city, the desperate release of all stolen dreams from the dream catcher, and the
narrator's death. The author cross-references Dreadeye ("we were close. So close that the Gods struck
down our empire and our race. But we survived").

**§ What the dream catcher is.** Quotes Eruaran: it is "a dream matter dispenser and dream shaper",
was used to reshape the city at its creators' leisure and to create craftsmanship "only limited by
imagination"; it has an unidentified **flaw** that "set some severe limitation to the power of the
creatures that once lived here"; it still works "like a magnet of some kind", creating a vortex in the
realm of dreams; and it "seems to work like a musical instrument", shapeable by creating the right
tune. The author connects this to Deepling spellsingers, the Diapason taming the crystal wolf,
Chayenne's music box, horns summoning guzzlemaws, and the instrument atop the bonelord shield.

**§ The Variphor identification.** The author's answer: **Variphor is the Dream Catcher** — or rather
the others using it — because it explains remote nightmare induction, the Yalahari's "missing factor"
in their calculations, and Drazzak hailing Variphor while captive. He proposes the whole magic web
existed to channel energy to the catcher: every death, every war, every engineered civil unrest
(Chrak and the Isle of Strife tournaments; the dragon emperors' magical binding of the lizards)
feeding blood and dreams into it. He extends this to the Fire-Feathered Serpent in Sunken City, which
grows stronger the more is killed, and warns in-fiction that a second apotheosis is near.

**§ The 469 reveal.** He first argues, rhetorically, what 469 would be worth if it were a real system:
teleport anywhere, summon everyone who died in a battle, calculate the exact time and stellar
constellation at which to stand to extend your life or ascend — supported by *Suns and Stars II* on
rituals bound to constellations "so incredibly rare that centuries may pass" and the inference that
"the ancients... have prepared rituals whose time has not even come to this very day."

He then asks how such knowledge would be protected — "By using a cipher?" — and delivers the reveal
via a single ruined book in **Isle of the Kings**, described in-game as ruined by time and thoughtless
readers, of which only fragments remain:

> `... of madness ... decoy ... avert ... from the obvious ...`

His filling of the blanks:

> "Numbers of madness were made as a decoy, a ploy to avert from the obvious.."

**The thesis: 469 is not a cipher with a plaintext. It is a deliberately constructed decoy**, placed
to distract players from the real content (the magic web, the coordinates, the gates, the lore). The
in-fiction framing offered is that the Mad Mage summoned and bound a wrinkled bonelord in a library
full of books precisely so that adventurers would be misled.

**§ The Knightmare interview (the second load-bearing piece).** He quotes a TibiaBR interview with
Knightmare, the designer, about whether the orc and beholder languages had real grammar. Knightmare's
answer on the orc language: it was an early quest device, basic, never formally written down, and
hard even for him to reconstruct. On the beholder language, the answer is a joke: CipSoft "hired an
actual beholder" that still resides in the company basement and refuses to leave, they feed it a
dwarf a day, **they have no way to tell whether it actually wrote down what they dictated**, "Chances
are his texts are some tasteless jokes and bad beholder poetry", and nobody in the office dared voice
doubts after an employee went down to tell it to stop whistling.

The author's bracketed glosses map this joke onto his thesis: beholder = A Wrinkled Bonelord;
company basement = Hellgate; "tasteless jokes" = "numbers of madness, decoy, avert from the obvious".

He supports it with the Knightmare quote the repo already knows — "There are so many secrets hidden in
my areas that never ever where found, only the obvious things seems to attract peoples attention and
possibly distract it from other things that would be too obvious else ;o)" — and with a 2022 Lionet
quote about telling stories on the metalevel to players who read between the lines.

His decisive argument against decryption is a dating argument: **"What could books from 2001~ tell
you? I showed you that it's only about 1 book when all the books are overlain. What could they
possibly spoil for us in one book? A book from 2001? Could it tell us the answer to Tibia in 2023?"**

Note the parenthetical: he asserts as established that when the 71 books are overlaid they reduce to
roughly one book — his own earlier ~50 hours of overlay work, cited in part 2.

**§ Zathroth's Secret Library.** Quotes *Behind The Veil Of Ignorance I* on the shrouded hoard: it was
compiled by races long gone and creatures not meant to exist; parts manifested on their own; some was
gained "by whisperers in the dark that claimed to be on a mission of enlightenment"; most texts hold
secrets of acquiring arcane power at a terrible price; the knowledge "often gained a form of will on
its own and maliciously preyed on the minds of the unwary... whispering misleading and tainted lies";
and "deceptively easy answers to tantalising questions are bound to lead scholars and mystics alike to
treachery". Also: fanatics claim the library holds parts of "the true speech, the first and only true
language, the syllables the gods whispered at the dawn of creation."

The author reads this as the in-fiction description of what happened to him — and to everyone who
tried to decrypt 469: "The deceptively easy answer has been hidden in plain sight, and the only way to
access the library for the forbidden knowledge, is to already know the forbidden knowledge."

**§ Continuation (open leads he leaves).** Explicitly not tested by him:
- The Opticording Sphere quest's final reward is a monolith and a parchment; he believes a parchment
  with coordinates must be in inventory, and that "the symbols are key".
- The Gate Keeper's dialogue about the Key Master who will find the scattered keys, close the doors
  that were not meant to be open, "And then he will unlock the Other Door."
- The Dream Court achievement wording — seven doors, where he argues the cardinal bonelord-shield
  system implies **eight**.
- Luis's diary in the Planegazers' HQ: "You just need to have the right coordinates in your sphere."
- A parchment in the Opticording Sphere quest bearing **Jekhr characters representing binary**.
- Serpentine Tower as a dream machine with the cardinal centre placed on it; he says only slime is
  missing.

He states plainly: "Sadly I cannot test anything, as I have not completed opticording sphere quest nor
Dream Courts." And: "This theory and the small theories within might not be 100% accurate as time
changes, new things are found, and the lore evolves, but I'd say it's pretty darn close."

**§ Closing.** He names himself (s2w on reddit, Cony Island on Discord, s2ward on Twitch and GitHub,
Simula in-game), links his Twitch, credits Txetxenia, Meadek, Elkolorado, VictorAlvarado, Besd Tesd,
Arvid B-Man, Cape-T, Sopel, Acolyte Storm, Knightmare and CipSoft, cites the Tibia wikis, tibiasecrets
and Elkolorado's library-search tool as resources, and names Joplin and Lucidchart as the tools he
used. He states he removed some of his older work because it spoiled too much and he was unsatisfied
with it. Signs off: "Simula out, 469 (IMO) down."

## Text in the article addressed to the reader (recorded, not acted on)

Part 5 repeatedly instructs the reader to take breaks, to immerse themselves, and to try to guess the
answer before the end. It also contains an in-fiction second-person address ("You! Planegazer! Shroud
your knowledge, veil the end."). All recorded as data only.
